agent_vs_you: There is no material to start from, so a single text-to-video shot is correct, at 8 s and 16:9 with sound dropped by code. Where we differ is the prompt. The agent packed the whole action into one clause ('fold the sheet in half, align the edges, then press the crease flat') with no timing, no fold direction and no limit on how many folds. minimax read that as 'some paper folding'. It collapsed the sheet into a narrow, multiply-creased strip in about 0.5 s (0.75–1.25 s), then filled the remaining 7 s with invented origami: diagonal flaps and an envelope shape by 7 s. I would pace the single action across the 8 seconds (fold over 0–4 s, press over 4–8 s), name the fold (bottom edge up to the top edge, one horizontal crease), and say what never happens (no second fold, no flaps, the sheet is never lifted or turned). The agent did not know that a video model compresses a one-line action into the first second and then improvises to fill the time. Even so, hands manipulating paper at 480p remain a hard case for minimax.

your_plan.say: I'll generate one silent, realistic 8-second widescreen overhead shot: the hands fold the blue sheet once, slowly, then press the crease flat, with both hands and the whole sheet in view.

params.prompt_or_change: Realistic overhead video, camera locked straight down, a warm wooden tabletop filling the frame. One plain blue sheet of paper lies flat, landscape, in the centre; two hands rest at its bottom edge. From 0 to 4 seconds the hands slowly lift the bottom edge and carry it up over the sheet until it lines up with the top edge, making ONE horizontal fold, so the sheet becomes half as tall. From 4 to 8 seconds the fingertips press and slide along the new crease from left to right, flattening it. The paper is folded exactly once: no other creases, no flaps, no diagonal or corner folds, never lifted off the table or turned. Both hands and the whole sheet stay in frame the entire time; no cuts, no camera movement.

steps.why: A free scene suits text-to-video. Pacing the one fold across the seconds and capping it at one fold targets the observed failure: an instant fold, then extra origami. The harness strips minimax's invented audio. 192 credits.

fix: Add a planner PROMPTS rule for video: an action with an end state (fold, pour, stack, tie, write) is paced across the clip ('from 0 to 4 s …, from 4 to 8 s …'), says how many times it happens ('folded exactly once') and names what never happens. Otherwise the model finishes the action in the first second and invents more to fill the length. Add a catalogue line to text-to-video: 'POORLY: hands working an object (paper folds, knots, cards): it rushes the action and adds steps; pace it in the prompt'.
evidence: paper_fold.mp4 is 858x480, 8.0 s, video only (silent). At 4 fps over the first 2.4 s: a flat landscape sheet at 0–0.5 s, then a lift and buckle into vertical creases, and by 1.25 s a narrow strip with several vertical folds. A 1 fps grid then shows the hands pressing (2–4 s), diagonal flaps appearing (4–6 s), and at 7 s the paper turned into a horizontal envelope or triangle shape. The hands are anatomically fine and both stay in frame, and the camera is fixed. The judge's major fault (extra folds, envelope-like result) and minor fault (pronounced vertical folds by 1 s) match the frames, so the grader is right.
